entities.name: FtsH protease
observations: Sequence is 642 aa and matches ATP-dependent zinc metalloprotease FtsH homologs with 62.4–65.5% identity and 91.7–97.7% query coverage.
Contains an N-terminal FtsH_ext region, predicted membrane-spanning segment(s), AAA+ ATPase domains, and a Peptidase_M41 metalloprotease domain.
Reference FtsH proteins are inner-membrane, cytoplasmic-side, homohexameric proteases involved in integral membrane-protein quality control.
Sequence-derived properties: molecular mass ~70.3 kDa; theoretical pI 5.26; net charge at pH 7 approximately -17.5.

entities.name: Membrane protein quality control
observations: FtsH homolog annotations describe ATP-dependent degradation and quality control of integral membrane proteins.

The process likely includes recognition, ATP-powered unfolding/translocation, and zinc-dependent proteolysis of selected membrane or cytoplasmic substrates; the mechanistic wording beyond the curated annotation is functional interpretation.

entities.name: ATP-dependent proteolysis
observations: Reference homologs are annotated with ATP binding, ATP hydrolysis, ATP-dependent peptidase activity, metalloendopeptidase activity, and protein catabolic process.
The sequence contains a conserved P-loop region, VGPPGTGKT, supporting an AAA+ ATPase motor.

entities.name: Bacterial inner membrane
observations: Reference FtsH homologs are annotated as cell inner-membrane, multi-pass membrane proteins with the catalytic machinery on the cytoplasmic side.
The query has a strongly hydrophobic N-terminal segment and a second hydrophobic region around residues 100–150, consistent with an N-terminal membrane anchor.

entities.name: AAA+ ATPase
observations: Pfam AAA and AAA_5 domains span approximately residues 191–323; the sequence contains the Walker-A-like motif VGPPGTGKT.
This module supplies ATP-dependent mechanical activity for FtsH proteolysis.

entities.name: Peptidase M41
observations: Pfam Peptidase_M41 spans approximately residues 404–594, consistent with the zinc metalloprotease domain of FtsH.
Reference annotations support zinc ion binding and metalloendopeptidase activity.
